Title: The History of the Evangelical Churches of the Valleys of Piemont
Creator: Samuel Morland (Sir Samuel Morland, 1625-1695), Cromwell's Commissioner Extraordinary for the affairs of the Valleys
Publisher: London: printed by Henry Hills for Adoniram Byfield
Publication Date: 1658
Rights: Public Domain (printed in London in 1658; public domain by date under the project's 95-year rule)
Source: Internet Archive item historyofevangel00morl, file historyofevangel00morl_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the library/source-research thread (Era VII session), 2026-10-16; host rights statement: the item carries no possible-copyright-status field and no access-restricted-item flag; contributor Princeton Theological Seminary Library (Collection of Puritan and English Theological Literature).
Provenance note: Header prepended; the OCR text follows unchanged (no characters altered; the raw file contains 0 long-s glyphs, so no long-s normalisation was done; the OCR itself renders the 1658 long s as the letter f throughout, e.g. 'moft', 'thofe', and that is left exactly as scanned). Rights basis restated: a book printed in London in 1658 is public domain by date.
Content note: Whole volume in three Books. Book I (chapters I-VIII, from 'BOOK I.' in the file): geography of the valleys, the ancient and modern belief with the confessions of faith including the brief Confession made at Angrogna 12 September 1532, the ancient discipline, extracts of the ancient treatises in the valleys' own language (the Nobla Leyczon and others) with English, and the discourse on the Barbes. Book II ('SECOND BOOK OF THE HISTORY'): the persecutions, the Order of Gastaldo of 1655, the supplications, and the narrative of the 1655 massacre with the copies of the depositions and attestations. Book III ('THIRD BOOK OF THE HISTORY'): the Swiss mediation, Cromwell's letters, Morland's own negotiation, the collection in England, the treaty of Pignerol and its grievances to 1658; many documents are printed in French and Italian with English. The Princeton copy lacks gathering Mmmm4 (two pages) by the item's own signature statement. OCR sampled at 10/30/50/70/90% and found readable English and French with long s as f throughout and occasional broken words; exact wording must be checked against the page image before quotation, so this file is a second witness for wording until a cleaner scan is vendored.

Of  the  Fear  of  the  Lord. 

THe  fear  of  the  Lord  drives  away 
fin.  By  the  fear  of  the  Lord  is 
procured  much  good  .    As  Solomon 
laith.  The  fear  of  the  Lord  is  the  begin- 
ning of  wifdom.   And  again ,  Happy 
is  the  man  that  always  thus  fears.  For 
by  the  fear  of  the  Lord  his  Soul  is 
delivered  from  the  pains  of  Hell,  and 
by  the  fear  ot  the  Lord  he  findesthe 
joys  of  Heaven.  The  Love  ot  God 
and  of  our  Neighbour ,  is  Charity 
and  he  that  has  Charity,  is  of  God 
and  he  that  is  of  God,  is  weaned  from
